name: Timna
overview: Timna was a male Edomite who held the significant position of chief of Edom, as recorded in Genesis 36:40. His leadership role marks him as an important figure within the Edomite tribe. There are no additional personal notes or details about his life beyond this unique attribute.
namesAndTitles: The name Timna means 'lot' or 'portion' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name given without direct attribution to God. This meaning is noted in Genesis 36:40 but does not elaborate further on his character or role.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture indicates that Timna was a descendant of Esau, which connects him to the broader lineage of Edomites. Beyond this, no other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Timna's significance lies in his role as a chief of Edom, highlighting the structured leadership among Esau's descendants. His mention in Genesis 36:40 situates him within the genealogical and tribal history important to understanding the nations related to Israel. Though brief, his record contributes to the biblical account of Edomite chiefs and their place in God's providential plan.
